subject.title: fix(cron): respect deliveryBestEffort in interim-message suppression guard

question: Should `deliveryBestEffort` intentionally allow an unchanged interim acknowledgement to be delivered while descendant runs are genuinely active, or should the fix be narrowed to stale/inactive descendant state only?
rationale: Current main has an explicit focused regression expectation that best-effort still suppresses stale interim text while descendants run, while two sibling best-effort branches and the contributor’s evidence support a broader interpretation. This is a user-visible cron delivery-policy choice that source inspection available in the supplied context cannot safely resolve.

options.title: Preserve active-run suppression
options.body: Keep the current active-descendant safeguard and implement a separate stale-state repair or a narrowly proven inactive-state exception.

options.title: Adopt deliver-immediately semantics
options.body: Accept that best-effort jobs may send interim text during active descendant work and merge this change with an explicit maintained contract and user-visible regression coverage.

recommendation.title: Preserve active-run suppression
recommendation.body: Keep the current active-descendant safeguard and implement a separate stale-state repair or a narrowly proven inactive-state exception.

likelyOwner.reason: This person was explicitly asked to resolve the precise delivery-policy question in the PR discussion.
